explanation: The Wilton article makes the 1690 raid the reason the 1693 one could be found at all: "In sixteen days they reached the Mohawk, led by a guide captured in the Schenectady Massacre, Jan Baptiste Van Eps." The same man then undid it: "Van Eps had escaped before the attacks and made his way to Schenectady, where he alerted the inhabitants to the French attack". That is how Schuyler came to be on the retreat road. The link is enabled: Schenectady supplied the man who led the way to the Mohawk castles. It did not decide that the castles would be attacked. Wikipedia is the only author named, so probable.
